🎵 TikTok Growth Guide · Lesson 3 of 5

Trends Bring Spikes, Search Brings Months

5 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

"Search value" isn't creator slang. It's TikTok's own term, and it's one of the four things TikTok's Creator Rewards Program uses to decide which videos are worth paying for.

TikTok described search value as a metric based on popular search terms. In plain English: TikTok tracks whether your video answers things people actually type. That tells you where the platform is heading. Trends get you a spike; search gets you views for months.

Trends: borrow the format, keep your voice

The accounts that grow from trends don't copy them. They take the format (the sound, the transition, the joke structure) and fill it with their own niche. A trending "things I'd never buy again" sound becomes "3 mitumba bales I'd never buy again" for a Gikomba seller.

Trend elementCopy it?Make it yours by
The sound or beatYes, early in its lifeSpeaking your own line over it, or using it under your own footage
The joke or formatYesSwapping in a situation only your audience would get
The exact scriptNoWriting it for your niche: your prices, your area, your customers
The lookPartlyKeeping your usual framing so viewers recognise you

Search: the tool most creators never open

TikTok has a feature called Creator Search Insights. Type that phrase into the TikTok search bar (it's available in selected regions). It shows what people are searching for, and labels some topics "content gap": things people search for often but that have relatively few videos answering them.

💡 What most creators miss

A content gap is the closest thing TikTok gives you to a guaranteed audience. Someone is already typing the question; almost nobody has answered it. If Search Insights isn't available in your app, do the manual version: type your niche into the search bar and read the autocomplete suggestions. Each one is a real question from real people.

✗ MYTH

Hashtags are how TikTok knows what your video is about.

✓ REALITY

Hashtags help, but they are only one piece of 'video information'. Your caption, the words on screen and what you say out loud all help TikTok match the video to searches. A caption that says "Sunday vibes" tells search nothing. "Pilau for 4 people under KES 600" tells it everything.

📋 Search-first opener
Say in the first 2 seconds: "[WHAT PEOPLE SEARCH] in [TOWN/AREA], here's [WHAT YOU'LL SHOW]."
On-screen text: [WHAT PEOPLE SEARCH]
Caption: [WHAT PEOPLE SEARCH] | [PRICE IN KES / TIME / RESULT]. [QUESTION FOR COMMENTS]?
Example: "Knotless braids price in Nairobi, here's what KES 3,500 gets you."
  • Post a steady number of videos you can keep up for a month. Consistency you can sustain beats a burst of daily posts that burns you out.
  • Keep one recognisable thing across videos: a catchphrase, a sign-off, a colour. Trends bring strangers; your signature makes them remember you.
✅ Do this today
⚡ Quick check

In TikTok's Creator Search Insights, what does a "content gap" label mean?

TikTok defines content gap topics as ones searched often but answered by relatively few videos. That's demand waiting for supply, the easiest search traffic you'll ever get.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. 'Search value' is an official TikTok metric in Creator Rewards.
  2. Copy a trend's format, never its script.
  3. Creator Search Insights flags 'content gap' topics with demand and few answers.
  4. Say, show and caption the exact phrase people search.
